- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 2–5% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior 5-day avg), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast peak at 10–15% above prior high.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, forecast should not continue downward beyond 1–2% below recent low.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; apply smoothing filter: average last 3–5 forecast values before applying sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 → 0.67), model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
